w: Kishore Day
During Swamishri's puja, kishores sang bhajans with the accompaniment of instruments.

The evening program presentations included a traditional, colorful dance, singing of kirtans and an interesting discussion about the divine, redemptory attributes of Swamishri. The kishores then sang a bhajan "Chhana, chhana, chhana tame kya sudhi chhana rehesho." Then they asked Swamishri to reveal his true form to them. In his blessings Swamishri began, "I am a sadhu of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the servant of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj and my name is Narayanswarupdas..."

The Guru Punam assembly commenced with bhajans and speeches by sadhus. Pujya Viveksagar Swami, Pujya Doctor Swami and Pujya Mahant Swami discoursed about the glory of the guru tradition in India and the divinity of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. The program was interlaced with bhajans and with colorful folk dances by kishores. When a light rainshower started Swamishri was requested to stop it because 35,000 devotees had assembled for the festival. Swamishri looked at the sky and the rain stopped immediately, but it poured heavily in the neighboring villages of Rudel, Dharmaj, Borsad, Dabhasi, etc. Finally, Swamishri blessed the Guru Punam assembly, "... Generally people do not like talks related to God or satsang. We do not like going to satsang. Our senses and mind do not like satsang, it is only the jiva that likes it. One has to remove one's base instincts, worldly desires, ego and attachment for worldly things. Only when this dirt is removed can one experience peace and happiness within... I pray on this day of Guru Punam that may God remain foremost in our souls. May spiritual knowledge be consolidated in our lives. And may there be peace everywhere..."

Kishore - Kishori Din In the evening, during the main Kishore-Kishori Din programme, kishores presented a drama that illustrated the main problems they face in the school environment and the role of personal satsang as the solution to these problems. In his blessings, Swamishri stated that the values and culture prevalent in India must also be practiced here. He also emphasised satsang and education, and the loving relationship that must be cultivated between parents and their children.

While Swamishri was performing his morning puja, the vice-president of India, H.E. Bhaironsinh Shekhavat arrived for darshan. After puja the vice-president was given a tour of the under construction Swaminarayan Akshardham and then he returned to meet Swamishri.

ds.t: Come, let us go to Akshardham
w: Wednesday, 13 July 2005 (Ashadh sud 6, Samvat 2061), Delhi
... Brahmavihari Swami: "None of us has any skill. Only you teach everyone, give strength and do the work."
Aksharprem Swami: "In your name even stones would float."

With a gentle smile, looking at the murti of Maharaj, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "It is all His glory. It happens by His strength. It happens only by His strength. To believe Him to be the doer too, that is our principle."
"But Bapa! When we fail, we cannot believe that," said Paramtattva Swami.

"That is exactly our principle." Going on, Swamishri said, "If we succeed, it is He (Maharaj), and if we fail, it is still He. And in fact, God never gives us failure. Even in what may look like failure, there is only success. The work does not happen only if some big obstacle was going to come. God protects us. But (smiling, playing his finger in his palm) to see success in failure is very difficult." Having said this, he repeated it: "It is very difficult. We think, 'I failed, so what about my reputation? What will people say?' Caught up in this one gets confused and gives up. But God alone is the doer of all."

ds.t: A meeting moved to the evening
w: The BAPS Swaminarayan mandir in Uganda was completing 50 years. On the occasion of the 'Golden Jubilee Festival' being celebrated for this, leading devotees of the East Africa Satsang Mandal had come here to invite Pramukh Swami Maharaj to Africa. A special meeting with them had been scheduled for tomorrow morning. This evening Swamishri said, "If no one is leaving, let us hold the meeting in the evening, because in the morning there is less time."
As Swamishri suggested, all the members were asked, and everyone was happy.

In this context, as the talk went on, Swamishri said, "The feelings of every devotee should be looked after. It is because feelings have been looked after that satsang has grown so much; everyone has been listened to. How Yogiji Maharaj looked after everyone! In the same way, looking after the devotees is a great seva."

This evening Pramukh Swami Maharaj called the devotees who had served with body, mind and wealth for the new sanctum of Akshardham, and personally draped a shawl over each of them. Among these devotees, Harishbhai Bhuptani, who had come from Kampala, came to Swamishri and said, "Salutations to the one who shows us Brahmadham."
Swamishri said, "Your devotion is like that, and may that devotion keep growing. My blessings that your devotion keeps growing along with understanding of the glory."
Harishbhai said, "Please bless us that our whole family is coloured by satsang."
Swamishri said, "Slowly, slowly it will happen."
Harishbhai said, "But where is there that much time?"
Kishorbhai Bhuptani said, "Does it happen through effort, through destiny or through grace?"

Swamishri said, "Only when there is grace do we attain God and the Sant. While doing devotion, grace also comes. Maharaj will certainly shower grace on all of you, and your boat will reach the other shore."

Yesterday, at the inauguration of the new sanctum, Bhadresh Swami, the organisation's scholarly sadhu, composed verses describing the unique sanctum and offering heartfelt salutations to Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Today, while offering the meal to Thakorji, Pramukh Swami Maharaj saw Bhadresh Swami sitting in front and said, "You composed good verses, but nothing about Yogiji Maharaj came in them. So compose verses about Yogiji Maharaj too."
On Swamishri's instruction he immediately composed verses in the anushtup metre:
The building of Akshardham was the wish of Yogi Swami;
Pramukh, loving to his guru, fulfils it with devotion.
To Pramukh, our guru in person, salutations again and again,
By whom this grand Akshardham, giver of liberation, has been made.
Swamishri was pleased and gave him as prasad the three laddus placed in the thal.

Harishbhai said, "But where is there so much time?"
Kishorbhai Bhupatani said, "Does it happen through effort, through destiny or through grace?"
Swamishri said, "Only through grace does one meet Bhagwan and the Sant. By doing devotion, grace also comes. Maharaj will surely bestow his grace on all of you, and you will be taken across."

Yesterday, on the occasion of the inauguration of the new sanctum, Bhadresh Swami, a learned sant of the organisation, had composed verses offering heartfelt salutations to Bhagwan Swaminarayan together with a description of the unique sanctum. Today, while offering food to Thakorji, Pramukh Swami Maharaj saw Bhadresh Swami sitting in front and said, "You composed good verses, but there was nothing about Yogiji Maharaj in them. So compose verses about Yogiji Maharaj too."
At Swamishri's command, he immediately composed verses in the anushtup metre.
Yogi Swami had the wish to build Akshardham;
Pramukh, loving to his guru, fulfils it with devotion.
To Guru Pramukh, in person, salutations again and again,
By whom this grand Akshardham, giver of liberation, was created.
Swamishri was pleased and gave him the prasad of three laddus placed in the thal.

Today, after performing abhishek in the Abhishek Mandapam, Mahant Swami Maharaj sat in a chair to put on his socks. So that Swamishri's special glance falls on it, a sentence or so is usually written where Swamishri's feet will be.
Today it said there: "Just as Bapa (Pramukh Swami Maharaj) said 'I love you all,' you too have said 'I love you all' to everyone."
Swamishri stood up and, showing his dislike of this practice, said, "Do not do this. My feet fall on it."
The attendant sadhu said, "But it has been written here precisely so that the great sadhu's feet fall on it."
Swamishri said, "If it were my name, it would not matter, but this was Bapa's (Pramukh Swami Maharaj's) name."
What subtle devotion to the guru! His feet should not fall on his guru's name even by mistake.
Today Mahant Swami Maharaj came up into the mandir and, arriving at the shrine of Bhagatji Maharaj, said happily, "I had wished for a khes (shawl worn over the shoulder), and the khes has come."
Bhagatji Maharaj had been dressed in a pink khes. So the attendant sadhu asked, "Was the wish for a pink khes?"
Swamishri said, "No, every day there was no khes at all;
it was bare."
The attendant sadhu said, "He has been dressed in a khes like in Sarangpur."
Swamishri said, "No, there was one in Atlanta too."
This exchange of three or four sentences shows how minutely Swamishri has darshan.
Today, as every day, a reading from Yogi Vani began during the walk. In it came the talk that "Yogi Bapa explains Vachanamrut Gadhada II 56: 'From our side' means Aksharbrahman is included in it."
Clarifying it, Mahant Swami Maharaj said, "If Maharaj had said 'from my side,' it would be Maharaj alone, but he said 'from our side,' so Aksharbrahman is included."
Next came: "Until one has knowledge of the atma and Paramatma, one is not a true satsangi."
Swamishri said emphatically, "A satsangi, yes, but not a true satsangi."
Another talk came: "What is attachment to sense pleasures? When one has taken a vow and then, on getting a pleasure one likes, gives up the vow."
Going deeper, Swamishri said, "Or even if the thought arises in the mind, it is called attachment to sense pleasures."
